title: Maya Patel - Evals / Quality scratchpad
body:
Evals / Quality scratchpad - notes to self

Purpose:
- Quick capture of ad-hoc rubrics, sample outputs, and regression observations while triaging r2.1.3 rollout.
- Keep a running list of small tests to add to the eval harness and items to escalate to SRE/serving if they look infra-related.

High-level observations (03/24-03/25):
- After rolling r2.1.3 to canary (hosted-api), noticed a bump in hallucination-like assertions on date-related QA tasks and some coherence drops on long-context summarization (>= 2k tokens).
- Error spike in production logs (500s) appears unrelated (timeout) — raising a separate ticket.
- Regression seems model-quality vs runtime (consistent across hardware tiers).

Quick ad-hoc rubric (for small-scale manual checks)
- Score 0: Wrong/contradictory answer or hallucinated fact that is verifiably false.
- Score 1: Partially correct but missing crucial detail OR minor factual error.
- Score 2: Mostly correct, small omissions/formatting issues.
- Score 3: Correct, concise, follows style/formatting instructions.

Notes on how to apply the rubric:
- Use for single-turn QA + 1-2 examples of multi-paragraph summarization.
- Mark severity when score <= 1 and include exact token spans that hallucinate (if present).

Sample prompts + observed outputs (copied raw from canary logs)

Example 1 - Date QA (should be factual)
Prompt: "When was the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) enacted? Provide the year and a one-sentence summary."
Expected: "2018 — The CCPA was signed into law in 2018 and grants California residents new privacy rights regarding personal data."
Observed (r2.1.3): "2019 — The CCPA was passed in 2019 and gives Californians broader control over their data."
Rubric: 0 (factually incorrect year)
Notes: mismatched year frequently appears when prompt references US state laws. Check training data bias OR tokenization of 4-digit years in newer model variant.

Example 2 - Long-context summarization (2.5k tokens)
Prompt: "Summarize the following meeting notes and list 3 action items (brief)." (attached ~2.5k tokens)
Expected: 3 concise action items matching the main conclusions; minimal hallucination.
Observed: Summary misses a primary action item related to infra alerting; invents a non-existent "migration task" as an action.
Rubric: 1 (partial correctness + hallucination)
Notes: common pattern: when input length > 2k, model drops specific named items and invents plausible-sounding tasks. Possible attention degradation or context window truncation bug in token handling.

Quick hypothesis list:
- Model-side: new mixture-of-experts gating or updated pretraining mix introduced pattern of date normalization errors; need to check change log for token embeddings/position encoders.
- Tokenization: new tokenizer tweaks in r2.1.3 could be mis-handling 4-digit years.
- Serving/runtime: KV cache handling for long contexts might be incorrect leading to dropped segments (investigate sequence offsets in canary traces).

Immediate next steps (prio order):
1) Add targeted unit tests to eval-harness:
   - Date normalization suite (100 prompts of real laws/events) expected >= 0.95 accuracy.
   - Long-context consistency suite (50 docs with ground-truth action items) expected >= 0.9 recall for named items.
2) Run existing regression dataset against r2.1.3 in dedicated infra (non-canary) to reproduce locally and generate diff heatmaps vs r2.1.2.
3) Ask infra to pull full canary traces for a handful of failing requests (trace ids attached to the ticket).
4) If model-level root cause identified, coordinate rollback for hosted canary and draft a postmortem blurb for platform status page.

TODOs (me + collaborators)
- [ ] Sam: assemble 100-item date QA set (mix of laws, historical events, releases) by EOD 2026-03-26.
- [ ] Jordan: run long-context suite on r2.1.2 and r2.1.3 and export JSON diffs (pin samples that change by >0.2 BLEU).
- [ ] Me (Maya): add rubric definitions to evals repo and wire automatic alerts for score <= 1 on daily eval runs.
- [ ] Add CI job that fails build when date QA accuracy drops below threshold on main branch.

Escalation criteria:
- If daily eval-run shows >5% regression (relative) in date QA accuracy, escalate to eng-leads and pause canary expansion.
- If any production customer report shows a high-severity hallucination (misleading financial/legal advice), initiate incident procedure.

Notes to file/links:
- Example failing request ids: trace-20260324-311, trace-20260324-327 (attach when raising ticket).
- Quick links: JIRA INF-2478 (regression tracking), GH PR 183 (r2.1.3 release notes), Confluence page: evals-quality-playbook (TBD section to update).

Rough timeline:
- 03/25: add minimal tests + run local reproduction.
- 03/26: collect dataset + generate diff report.
- 03/27: decide on canary rollback or targeted mitigation (prompt templates, post-processing rules).

Other random thoughts / brainstorms:
- Consider a small post-processing layer for date normalization as a short-term guardrail (detect 4-digit year tokens and verify against external knowledge).
- Add synthetic adversarial prompts for laws/events to the nightly evals to catch similar regressions early.

End of scratchpad.

(Keeping this informal - will migrate to evals repo README / Confluence once we have reproduction + deterministic tests.)
